background.source: India, officially known as the Republic of India, is a country located in South Asia. It is the seventh-largest country and the second-most populous country in the world. It has land borders with Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar, and maritime borders with Thailand, Myanmar, and Indonesia. India has a diverse population, with settlers arriving on the subcontinent from Africa over 55,000 years ago. Settled life emerged on the subcontinent 9,000 years ago, eventually evolving into the Indus Valley Civilisation. Hinduism dawned in India from the Rigveda, which was preserved by a vigilant oral tradition. Stratification and exclusion by caste emerged within Hinduism, and Buddhism and Jainism arose, proclaiming social orders unlinked to heredity. Early political consolidations gave rise to the loose-knit Maurya and Gupta Empires. The Mughal Empire ushered in two centuries of relative peace, leaving a legacy of luminous architecture. India became a colony of the British East India Company and eventually gained independence after an influential nationalist movement emerged, which was noted for nonviolent resistance. India has since become a federal republic and a fast-growing major economy. It has a space programme and plays an increasing role in global culture. However, India also faces various socio-economic challenges, including gender inequality, child malnutrition, and rising levels of air pollution. India is megadiverse, with four biodiversity hotspots and a wildlife population supported in protected habitats. The item's keywords, Indian River, Indus script, and Buddhism, are part of India's rich history and cultural heritage.
background.target: Ancient Greece was a civilization situated in the northeastern Mediterranean, which lasted from the Greek Dark Ages until around 600AD. It was composed of various city-states, largely unified under Alexander the Great. Classical Greece, which spanned from the 5th to 4th centuries BC, was considered the Golden Age of Athens and had a lasting impact on Western civilization, particularly in philosophy, politics, science, and art. The influence of Greek culture even extended to ancient Rome, which carried it throughout the Mediterranean and Europe. The Aegean Sea played a significant role in the formation of Greek urban poleis in the 8th century BC, marking the beginning of the Archaic period and the colonization of the Mediterranean Basin. The Greek alphabet, an essential element of their legacy, was adopted and disseminated throughout the Mediterranean world.
